text: Fire runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the big ask you make before fear catches up, the quiet party that comes alive when you walk in, and the emergency you head for while others look for their coats.

findings.issue: A General image (the crisis) on the Rival's edge. Nothing in the Rival's 40 passages heads for emergencies.
findings.auditor_note: Rewrite the field: "Fire runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the big ask you make before fear catches up, the quiet party that comes alive when you walk in, and the bid you raise because someone else wants the same prize."

text: You wait to feel ready rather than work to be ready, and getting ready never ends. With more Earth than your core uses, you choose another round of preparing over a first attempt. You are allowed to make the first attempt before the feeling arrives.

findings.issue: The cause is the chart's arithmetic, not the reader's need (D10, the owned cause). The prose should carry no astrology (benchmarks §1.2). This is the only K2 passage on the 30 pages that does it, and it sits on the golden chart. The house's own exemplar for this chip (benchmarks §4: "Getting ready is where you feel most in control") is stronger than the live text. "first attempt" also appears twice.
findings.auditor_note: "You wait to feel ready rather than work to be ready, and getting ready never ends. Preparing is the part you control, so you choose another round of it over a first attempt. You are allowed to start before the feeling arrives." (42)
findings.owner_approved: Preparing is the part you control, and you choose another round of it over a first attempt.

text: Protecting the people you love is the first thing you do with news. Because you treat their safety as your job, you protect them from a risk rather than watch them take it. You get to let them take their own risks.

findings.issue: A weak, slightly odd permission close: "get to let" and "take … risk" twice. It is the last word on the golden page's final keyword.
findings.auditor_note: "Protecting the people you love is your first move with news. Because you treat their safety as your job, you shield them from a risk rather than watch them take it. You are allowed to stand beside them and let the risk be theirs." (44)

text: Spreading yourself thin keeps you from being caught out and keeps you tired. You give each venture enough to stay in rather than enough to win, since quitting feels like losing. You run all of them on the one body you have.

findings.issue: "keeps you from being caught out" is unclear: caught out doing what?
findings.auditor_note: "Spreading yourself thin feels safer than betting on one thing, and it keeps you tired. You give each venture enough to stay in rather than enough to win, since quitting feels like losing. You run all of them on the one body you have." (44)
findings.owner_approved: Spreading yourself thin feels safer than betting on one thing, and it keeps you tired.

text: Saying too much proves to you that you were listening. Since a held tongue feels like a wasted turn, you spend your standing on the extra line instead of the needed one. You talk away trust that comes back slower than it left.

findings.issue: The cause does not fit the act; the Virtuoso talks to show what they have, not that they heard.
findings.auditor_note: "Saying too much proves to you that you have something to add. Since a held tongue feels like a wasted turn, you spend your standing on the extra line instead of the needed one. You talk away trust that comes back slower than it left." (45)

text: You rewrite a rule that stops making sense under the people standing on it. Since you fix it rather than keeping the peace, you change the footing with no warning. The rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.

findings.issue: A garden-path opener. Keep the excellent "somebody's floor".
findings.auditor_note: "When a rule stops making sense, you rewrite it, even with people standing on it. Since you fix it ahead of keeping the peace, the footing changes with no warning. You forget that the rule you found pointless was somebody's floor." (41)

text: Where you shut people out, you shut out what you were saving yourself for. Your own company works so well that you mistake it for the plan rather than a break. You pay for that peace in closeness, one quiet evening at a time.

findings.issue: The opener is opaque: what was being saved, and for what?
findings.auditor_note: "Shutting people out feels like rest to you, and it works too well. Your own company is so easy that you mistake it for the plan rather than a break. You pay for that peace in closeness, one quiet evening at a time." (43)

text: To win, you spend what is not only yours. You would rather cover the whole bill than split it, and you spend money your partner set aside for the two of you. Along with the money, you spend a plan you made together.

findings.issue: "spend" appears 4 times. "money your partner set aside" implies taking what is not yours, a bad-faith charge that BIZ_04's too-harsh test rules out. "To win" never says what is being won.
findings.auditor_note: "Winning the room matters enough that you pay for it with shared money. You would rather cover the whole bill than split it, even from savings meant for two. You spend a plan you made together along with the cash." (40)

text: You feel every loss as a blow to your standing. You would rather sit out a contest than risk losing it, because your standing feels at stake. You carry each loss for weeks after the contest itself is over.

findings.issue: Sentence 2's reason restates sentence 1. "standing" and "contest" each appear twice. On P075, "You carry each loss" echoes "You carry each problem alone" two passages up.
findings.auditor_note: "You feel every loss as a blow to your standing. Since a loss says something about you, you would rather sit out a contest than risk it. You replay each defeat for weeks after the game is over." (38)

text: Your best thinking happens alone, and you go off to it without saying how long. Thinking best out of reach, you let the solo hours run long rather than stop early. The people waiting on you never know when to expect you back.

findings.issue: "best thinking" then "Thinking best" says it twice, and "long" appears 3 times. The close is garbled.
findings.auditor_note: "Your best thinking happens alone, and you go off to it without saying how long. Since you think most clearly out of reach, you let the solo hours run on. You leave the people waiting with no idea when to expect you." (42)

text: Saying no has never come easily to you. Helping feels more like you than resting does, and you say yes before checking the cost. You owe no one a reason for saying no.

findings.issue: The next passage on the same page says "Taking it easy feels better than taking it on", so the reader is both the one who never rests and the one who drifts. The close also answers a guilt ("owe no one a reason") that the passage never raised.
findings.auditor_note: "Saying no has never come easily to you. A yes keeps the evening warm and everyone pleased, so you agree before you check what it costs. You never had to buy your place with a yes."

text: Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. You take a good time now sooner than a promise kept later, and you spend the house money on the evening. You take their share and leave them short on plans made together.

findings.issue: "House money" is a gambling idiom (winnings you can afford to lose), so it does not mean shared money. Two sentences open on "You take", and "take their share" reads as a charge of taking.
findings.auditor_note: "Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. A good time now feels surer than a promise kept later, so you spend on the evening what was meant for the plan. You leave them short on what you had agreed together."

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: You need an audience more than you need to be right. Being seen is how you know you exist, and you take being watched doing badly over doing well alone. Remember that you are just as real with no one watching.

findings.issue: The sentence has to be read twice to parse.
findings.auditor_note: "You need an audience more than you need to be right. Being seen is how you know you exist, so you would rather do badly in front of people than well on your own. Remember that you are just as real with no one watching."

text: Before anyone asks you to, you speak up for them. Having a voice comes more naturally to you than lending one, so you take the floor rather than handing it over. The quieter ones get heard in your words more than their own.

findings.issue: The passage opens on speaking up for others (lending your voice) and then charges the reader with not lending one. It contradicts itself.
findings.auditor_note: "Before the quiet ones find their words, you have said yours. Speaking comes more naturally to you than making room, so you take the floor before handing it over. Leave them the first word, since their turn is where you speak up."

text: You hate to lose more than you love to win, and the gap shows. You read a rival's win as your loss, since the Fire in you outlasts a single victory. You turn every friendly game into a fight and miss the fun of playing.

findings.issue: The opener is a famous sports quote, so it is not specific to the reader. The "since" clause does not explain why a rival's win reads as your loss, and the cause is chart talk, not the reader's need.
findings.auditor_note: "Losing stays with you far longer than winning does. A rival's win feels like a piece taken from you, so every friendly game becomes a fight to get it back. You win more often than most and enjoy the playing less."

text: Beside someone you like, you are all in unasked. You would sooner share the stake than check if they wanted one, so you double a bet that was theirs. Your money makes their plan bigger and riskier than they chose.

findings.issue: The stake/bet metaphor stands in for the action, so the reader has to decode it, and "bet" appears twice.
findings.auditor_note: "Beside someone you like, you go all in unasked. Sharing your energy feels like the best gift, so you double their plan without checking. Ask first, since you leave them a plan twice the size they chose."

text: Leaning on someone makes a hard thing feel lighter to you. Because another person's steadiness feels more reliable than yours, you lean on theirs rather than build any. You go without the one kind of strength you cannot borrow.

findings.issue: On the same page the reader "steps in ahead of being asked" to carry others. The protector and the leaner read as two people because the page never ties them together.
findings.auditor_note: "The care you give so freely is the care you lean on in return. Another person's steadiness feels safer than your own, so you lean on theirs rather than build any. You go without the one kind of strength you cannot borrow."

text: Your own needs come last whenever you are looking after someone. Because being needed feels easier than being tired, you give your rest away rather than keeping any. Your hobbies, friendships and plans all wait their turn behind everyone else's.

findings.issue: Being needed and being tired are not alternatives, so the cause does not parse. "Rest" also appears twice.
findings.auditor_note: "Your own needs come last whenever you are looking after someone. Being needed feels better to you than being rested, so you give your evenings away before keeping any. When you hold one back, you stop paying for everyone's comfort with your sleep."

text: You are harder on yourself than anyone else has been. With Fire past what your strength holds, you would sooner be hard on yourself than let one mistake go. You paid for each mistake the first time, and that was enough.

findings.issue: The cause is chart mechanics instead of the reader's own need, and "hard on yourself" appears twice in two sentences. The close is excellent and stays.
findings.auditor_note: "You are harder on yourself than anyone else has been. Letting a mistake go feels like letting yourself off, so you go over it long after everyone else has moved on. You paid for each mistake the first time, and that was enough."

text: Staying on duty is how you love the people in your care. Since being on duty comes easier than company, you give them a guard in place of someone to sit with. You keep them safe and leave them without the company they wanted.

findings.issue: "A guard ahead of someone" is awkward, and "company" and "duty" each appear twice.
findings.auditor_note: "Staying on duty is how you love the people in your care. Watching over them comes easier to you than sitting with them, so you stand guard where they wanted company. You keep them safe and miss the evenings they hoped to share with you."

text: Fire runs through your career, your health and your growth. It is the hard week that wakes you up, the body that finds its second wind when the stakes are real, and the test you pick yourself because that is where you grow.

findings.issue: This repeats the ledger's "Choose some of that pressure yourself" and pulls against the advice ("someone is allowed to tell you no").
findings.auditor_note: "Fire runs through your career, your health and your growth. It is the hard week that wakes you up, the body that finds its second wind when the stakes are real, and the deadline that gets more out of you than you planned to give."

text: You count everything, the money and the favours and the hours. Counting is your way of feeling safe, so knowing the total comes before enjoying the thing. You were only counting until it felt safe to enjoy what you have.

findings.issue: The past continuous suggests the counting has stopped, so the reader has to work out the meaning.
findings.auditor_note: "You count everything, the money and the favours and the hours. Counting is your way of feeling safe, so knowing the total comes ahead of enjoying the thing. You started counting so that one day you could enjoy what you have."

text: You hold back hardest where you love most. You keep a reserve rather than give it all, and your partner gets the careful share only. You leave your partner guessing at a warmth you have and never hand over.

findings.issue: "Never hand over" implies withholding on purpose. This is the concealment charge BIZ_04 rules out.
findings.auditor_note: "You hold back hardest where you love most. Keeping a reserve feels safer than giving it all, so your partner gets the careful share only. You feel more warmth than your partner ever gets to see."
findings.owner_approved: You feel more warmth than your partner ever gets to see.

text: Asking comes last, well after the point where it would have worked. You hold more of yourself than one load needs, and you carry all of it instead of owing anyone a piece. You are allowed to owe someone a piece of the load.

findings.issue: "hold more of yourself than one load needs" is abstract, and "owe … a piece" is said twice in two sentences.
findings.auditor_note: Asking comes last, well after the point where it would have worked. Owing anyone feels like losing ground, so you carry the whole load instead of sharing it. You are allowed to owe someone a piece of the load.

text: Doing it alone comes before any plan you make. Owing nobody feels safer to you, so you do the whole thing yourself sooner than hand off a piece. What you build is yours from the first nail to the last.

findings.issue: This repeats the friction pole's "Asks no one" (the same act, the same cause, the same "piece"), so the two poles do not differ in direction; it also closes on advice (W-001).
findings.auditor_note: Doing it alone is where your strength shows. You trust your own hands before anyone's plan, so you finish what others are still waiting on. You keep that strength with company beside you too.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: Where a sprint would get you in, you keep your pace instead. You would sooner be late on your terms than rushed on another's, since borrowed tempo is never yours. Some doors shut while you are still walking towards them.

findings.issue: "get you in" is unclear, "tempo" is above B2, and the reason goes round in a circle.
findings.auditor_note: When a sprint would get you there, you keep your own pace instead. Being late on your terms sits better with you than being rushed on someone else's. You lose the chances that needed a sprint, and you chose that trade.

text: Your biggest bets land on other people too. Going big matters more than going safe, and that puts the shared money at your size of risk. You risk their savings along with your own whenever you bet too big.

findings.issue: The close restates the chip and sentence 2, in the "along with your own" formula (pattern 6).
findings.auditor_note: Your biggest bets land on other people too. Going big matters more to you than going safe, so the shared money rides at your size of risk. You set the size of a risk that the people who pooled with you have to carry.

text: Thinking a question through means thinking it around, each side first. Being certain weighs more with you than being quick, so you take one more angle rather than decide. You never reach the decision in the middle of a circle, and it never closes alone.

findings.issue: It is unclear what "it" is (the circle? the decision?), and "never … never" blurs the cost.
findings.auditor_note: Thinking a question through means walking all the way around it first. Being certain weighs more with you than being quick, so you take one more angle rather than decide. You circle a question for weeks that a single choice would have closed.

text: You are spread among more things than your body keeps up with. Because letting go feels like losing rather than choosing, you spread yourself over them, tired at each one. Spread this thin, you never get a full rest and start each day already tired.

findings.issue: spread×4 and tired×2 in 43 words; the close restates sentence 2.
findings.auditor_note: You are spread over more things than your body can keep up with. Letting one go feels like losing, so you keep them all and arrive at each one tired. You never get a full rest, and you start each day already behind.

text: Spending on the people near you comes before your own next month. Because helping them out feels better than keeping, you spend on their short weeks rather than a shared cushion. You spend their quiet months as well as your own.

findings.issue: The reader cannot tell what "their quiet months" are; the cost to others does not land.
findings.auditor_note: Spending on the people near you comes before your own next month. Helping them out feels better than keeping, so you cover their short weeks instead of a shared cushion. You spend the savings that would have carried you both through a lean month.

text: Leaving comes hard to you, and you stay where the giving back stopped. You have more Wood than strength for it, so you stay rather than learn what leaving costs. You keep paying in effort every month to a place that returns none of it.

findings.issue: The logic is turned around: the reader stays because they fear what leaving costs, not to avoid learning it.
findings.auditor_note: Leaving comes hard to you, so you stay where the giving back stopped. With more Wood than strength for it, you put more in rather than face leaving. You keep paying in effort every month to a place that returns none of it.

text: You put comfort first for those in your care too. You would rather see a child happy now than stretched, so you pick pleasant hours over useful ones. You trade the effort they would grow on for an hour of ease.

findings.issue: A claim the reading cannot know: an 18 to 35 reader mostly has no child, and the line excludes them.
findings.auditor_note: You put comfort first for the people in your care too. You would rather see them happy now than stretched, so you pick pleasant hours over useful ones. You trade the effort they would grow on for an hour of ease.

text: Looking far comes naturally, and it pays. The next place is clearer to you than this one, so you see the far chance sooner than the near one. The opening right in front of you is the one you walk past most.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: Finishing is what you save for later. The last stretch costs you more than the first, and you open a new thing sooner than you close an old one. You leave the money and the credit sitting at the end you skip.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: Tired, you shut people out before anything else. Quiet is how you recover, and you shut people out sooner than ask for the quiet you need. You only ever wanted rest, never distance from the people you love.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: Spotting openings is what you do before anything is obvious. Carrying less Wood than drive to spend, you spot the far chance sooner than the one in your hand. Half the good ideas in your circle started as something you pointed at.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: With money, you spend sooner than you let it sit. Since spending feels like living and saving like waiting, you spend the whole month instead of keeping any. You pay for the free spending with savings you never get to keep.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: You change in front of an audience, for the better. Being watched is where your focus comes from, and you perform a thing sooner than you practice it. Your best work happens live, and the crowd gets all of it.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: What you make comes out without strain. Ease is the sign you trust, and you do the thing that flows sooner than you force the thing that counts. Your work has a lightness people feel at once.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.

text: You make hard things look easy. You show the finished thing sooner than the work, and you leave the people learning from you the ease without the steps. Anyone watching you sees how good the result can be.

findings.issue: "sooner than" used as a disguised "rather than" (owner approved the sweep with the MT-12 sample). Where it means time, it stays.
